sources.title: 2026 Income Tax Withholding Tables and Instructions for Employers, NC-30

employeeInputs.source: NC-4, NC-4 EZ, NC-4 NRA, or NC-4P

calculation.rounding: Round the final percentage-method or annualized-method withholding to the nearest whole dollar.
calculation.annualizedFormula: roundWholeDollar((max(0, wages * periodsPerYear - annualStandardDeduction - (allowances * 2500)) * 0.0409) / periodsPerYear) + additionalWithholding

whenRegularWagesHadWithholding: Apply 4.09% to separately identified supplemental wages
Or aggregate supplemental and most recent regular wages, compute combined withholding, and subtract withholding already taken from regular wages
supplementalWages.vacationPay: Treat as regular wages unless paid in addition to regular wages, in which case treat it as supplemental wages.
supplementalWages.tips: Treat reported tips as supplemental wages.

certificateRules.missingCertificate: Withhold as single with zero allowances.
certificateRules.priorYearExemptionExpires: Begin withholding on February 16 as single with zero allowances unless a new current-year certificate is supplied.

nonresidentAlienBranch.lowWageRule: When annualized wages do not exceed 12750, limit additional withholding to the lesser of the certificate amount or 4.09% of period wages.

residencyAndWorkRules.residentRule: North Carolina residents are generally subject on all wages wherever earned, but North Carolina withholding is not required for out-of-state services when that state requires withholding.
residencyAndWorkRules.nonresidentRule: Nonresidents are subject on wages allocated to services physically performed in North Carolina.

captureWarnings: The 36 pages of wage-bracket matrices are retained in the checksummed official source rather than duplicated into this source capture.
An executable implementation must preserve the prescribed whole-dollar final rounding and the separate nonresident-alien low-wage cap branch.

review.requiredNextStep: Implement percentage, annualized, supplemental, and nonresident-alien branches; test official and rounding-boundary examples; and independently compare representative wage-bracket rows before activation.
